subject.title: [Bug]: codex agent fails ("exited with code 1") — macOS XProtect deletes bundled @openai/codex@0.128.0 as malware; codex-acp@0.0.44 pins the flagged version

question: Should acpx resolve this by upgrading the built-in Codex adapter and documenting `CODEX_PATH`, or should it also automatically prefer or fall back to a `codex` executable found on PATH?
rationale: The adapter upgrade is a bounded compatibility change, while automatic PATH selection creates a lasting agent-specific executable-selection and trust convention that repository policy says must be deliberate.

options.title: Upgrade and document
options.body: Upgrade to a validated non-revoked codex-acp release, preserve stderr diagnostics, and document the explicit `CODEX_PATH` workaround without changing PATH trust behavior.

options.title: Add PATH recovery
options.body: Also inject or fall back to a PATH-resolved Codex executable, accepting the additional executable-selection and security policy surface.

recommendation.title: Upgrade and document
recommendation.body: Upgrade to a validated non-revoked codex-acp release, preserve stderr diagnostics, and document the explicit `CODEX_PATH` workaround without changing PATH trust behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The available merged history most directly connects this contributor to built-in registry coverage and CLI behavior.
